purpose: Test broad setting limits before locking faction approaches. Affiliations below are possibilities, not exclusive assignments.
review_policy: Only accepted designs enter the reference library. Rejects are deleted, including generated-source copies. Partial reviews may separate character, kit, magic and scale. Accepted references seed new invention, not a closed catalogue.

jobs.title: Return-stroke bracer
jobs.test: Can a small addition give a fighter control over impact without making the entire outfit magical?
jobs.lean: Open; scholarly craft usable by an independent fighter
jobs.notes: A compact brace catches the recoil of a heavy blow. Builds on the wardwright's useful addition while moving the idea toward physical fighters.
jobs.brief:
Input is reference for an economical meaningful magical addition and painted materials ONLY. Invent a new character, new mechanism, new pose and different clothing; do not copy blue plate, strings, floating rocks or the face.
Main: adult human woman about 38, solid muscular build, medium brown skin, broad crooked nose, uneven brow, dark hair cut to the jaw, appealing but ordinary experienced face. Full-body three-quarter pose facing LEFT, short charcoal padded jacket with a single plain iron collar, tan wool trousers, work boots, no cape or skirt armor. A two-handed workman's maul is held across the body immediately after an arrested downward practice swing; coherent hands and balanced legs, never aimed at viewer.
A SMALL blue-grey forged-steel brace over one forearm has one brass tension crescent and a simple hinged wrist support, only two useful fastenings. A short compressed amber-violet ripple at the wrist and maul head makes recoil visibly flow back into the brace. The effect is localized and powerful, not a superhero gauntlet or jet engine. No target, victim, scenery or debris storm.
Two detail studies: (1) removed brace, palm-side hinge and simple fit clearly shown; (2) complete modest iron-headed wooden maul beside a tiny painted study of the recoil wave. The brace should remain a modest addition to an ordinary person's equipment, not a full exosuit.

jobs.title: Rootwright's bending frame
jobs.test: Can cultivated living magic participate in skilled manufacture rather than oppose all industry?
jobs.lean: Open; nature craft meeting workshop practice
jobs.notes: A craftsperson coaxes a timber rib into shape on a restrained bending frame. Tests cooperation between living magic and manufacture, without making nature a factory aesthetic.
jobs.brief:
One sturdy waist-high oak bending bench, about three metres long, with exactly TWO large simple iron screw clamps and a removable curved timber former. A flexible freshly cut ash-wood strip is being drawn around the former into a useful boat/wagon rib; this is the main subject. One adult human craftsman, about 28, wavy dark hair, long nose, modestly handsome face, ordinary rolled green-grey linen shirt, dark apron and work trousers stands at the near end. Both hands are clearly placed on the wood while concentrating. He is not a tree person, automaton, elf stereotype or sage dressed in leaves.
A restrained luminous green-amber flow follows the wood grain near his palms; the rigid timber subtly bends and living fibres knit at a stress point. A few fresh buds remain at one end. The effect is alive and skilful rather than an electronic tracer, magical rope tying the object or explosive instant growth. Show careful hand work and useful iron tools coexisting with nature magic. No roots trapping the worker, forest background, irrigation or gardens.
Two details: (1) the resulting smooth curved timber rib, no ornate foliage, separated from the frame; (2) one clamp and the small repaired grain area showing the hand-sized glow, no scroll or wand required. Simple clear bench construction and human scale.

jobs.title: Resonance rolling mill
jobs.test: Can magic become a repeatable production process operated by a crew?
jobs.notes: Heavy rollers shape steel while a crew maintains a resonant treatment. Scales the loom's craft-and-magic relationship into production without enlarging its exact design.
jobs.brief:
Input references the successful meeting of real craft and luminous magic, ONLY; do NOT copy the loom, textile, parchment feed, tiny spools or silhouette.
A substantial industrial rolling mill about TEN metres long and FOUR metres high, shown fully on its own low stone foundation. Two massive forged dark-iron rollers in stout blue-grey iron uprights, oak drive wheels, ONE broad leather drive belt and one covered flywheel on the side. A thick heated steel slab enters the rollers and a flatter coherent sheet emerges onto aligned roller supports. All feed/support paths physically connect. No modern factory, electricity, lasers, gas cylinders, plastic, monitor or robot arms.
THREE ordinary adult human operators about 1.7 metres tall establish scale: one at the handwheel, one attending the entering slab with long tongs, one standing at a small side resonance rail. The last uses two plain metal rods against the rail; soft cyan-violet vibrations visibly pass through the rollers and steel, suggesting magically controlled tempering during real mechanical shaping. The metal remains metal, not a solid magic sheet, and there is no scroll-fed programming or glowing battery.
Two details: (1) a roller bearing and resonance rail, massive robust simple workmanship; (2) a short finished steel strip whose fine tempered grain catches a modest violet sheen. Neutral backdrop; no surrounding building or huge fiery atmosphere. Magic and labor both visibly participate.

jobs.title: Wind-keel freight barge
jobs.test: Can practical transport lift tonnes with magic, and what scale starts to feel too advanced?
jobs.lean: Open; craft, trade and independent travel
jobs.notes: A cargo barge rides just above the ground on an enchanted keel. A deliberate outer-edge test of transport capacity, rather than another small companion construct.
jobs.brief:
One original ten-metre-long freight vessel hovering only HALF A METRE above a simple neutral contact shadow, shown complete in a low three-quarter side view. Human-sized railings, a few ordinary tied cargo crates and TWO adult crew members on deck make scale unmistakable. It is a practical oak cargo barge with shallow flat hull, iron knees, a single short steering tiller at the stern and NO mast, balloon, wings, animal face, sail-fin, propeller, wheels, cannon or steam locomotive silhouette.
Beneath the hull, THREE broad smooth bronze runners form one coherent wind-keel. A pale, softly luminous silver-blue compression of air spreads beneath these runners, lifting the hull evenly. Visible magic reads as air under strain and thin painted eddies, not neon engine jets, antigravity sci-fi discs, solid light tentacles or a flying whale. One crew member adjusts a plain mechanical trim lever connected visibly to the keel; the other handles a mooring rope. No paper spells, gem batteries or unexplained pipe clusters.
Two details: (1) the keel bracket, one runner and its mechanical trim linkage; (2) stern tiller and a crew-sized boarding step. Well-built restrained fantasy craft. Neutral background with no city, river, landscape, map or other vessels. Its hovering freight function is an ambitious proposal, not established everyday travel.

jobs.title: Walking gantry - steam revision
jobs.test: Can a construct be major working infrastructure rather than a small autonomous helper?
jobs.notes: Steam-powered crane. A person directly supplies heat to the boiler; ordinary pressure, pistons and joints move the machine. No glowing magic joints.
jobs.brief:
A building-sized walking gantry approximately NINE metres high and twelve metres wide, shown COMPLETE on neutral paper. Exactly FOUR huge articulated load-bearing legs, widely spaced, support one broad arched iron-and-oak crane frame. No humanoid head, face, torso, claws, cute pet proportions or body armor. This is a made structure designed around its job. A narrow deck inside the arch contains a small clearly visible adult operator with a waist-high railing and sensible access ladder. A second human on the ground is the same actual scale.
An ordinary real chain hoist hangs from the centre, carrying a large cut-stone lintel between the legs. Chain, hook, beam weight and support path are physically coherent. A low cyan-violet magical shimmer inside the four knee joints suggests guided motive force; the operator's hands rest on two plain metal control bars. The machine does not need a glowing heart, scrolls, computer logic, exposed gears everywhere or giant holograms. One foot lifts only a little as it takes a slow heavy step; other three remain load-bearing. No floating whole structure.
Two details: (1) a single massive articulated foot and knee with the localized magical actuation, plus one tiny human-sized boot beside it for honest scale; (2) operator platform with simple control bars and intact railing. No quarry/city scenery, decorative rubble, battle, cannons or smoke. Serious industrial weight and restrained monumental invention.

jobs.revision_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Revise this Breachline WALKING GANTRY according to the creator's specific feedback: they find the crane interesting, but want it powered by STEAM, with perhaps a person using magic to heat the boiler. This is the only redesign requested now.
PRESERVE the large four-legged arched oak-and-dark-iron gantry, its full silhouette, scale, layout, central hanging chain and stone lintel, operator walkway, railing, ladder and the four existing load-bearing leg positions. Keep the warm off-white neutral background, selective traditional painted realism and the two-detail reference-sheet format. Humans remain normal sized next to the building-sized machine.
REPLACE ALL purple/cyan glowing knee gaps with solid ordinary mechanical pivot joints and substantial believable STEAM CYLINDERS with piston rods driving the legs. Put a SMALL NUMBER of useful metal steam lines along the structural members, clearly connecting to one compact horizontal riveted iron boiler mounted in an insulated steel cradle beside the existing upper operator platform. Do not make a walking locomotive or add a forest of pipes. Retain broad simple wood-and-iron construction. A few modest white steam wisps escape at a valve; no giant smoke cloud.
One human continues to operate the crane controls. A SECOND human caster beside the boiler reaches one BARE HAND toward the open insulated firebox, creating a compact natural-looking orange-white FLAME directly from their palm into the firebox. The person is the magical heat source. Steam pressure and ordinary piston linkages move the machine. NO magical glowing joints, magic batteries, enchanted steam, purple energy lines, luminous strings, ribbons, runic circuits, scroll cartridges or solid energy tubes. Show the magical input only as the caster's localized controlled flame and heat-light on the firebox.
RIGHT TOP DETAIL: replace the old glowing knee detail with a close view of a solid steel pivot, steam cylinder and piston linkage on the same leg, with a normal boot nearby for scale. RIGHT BOTTOM DETAIL: show the boiler/firebox and the human caster directly supplying flame with one hand, the rest of their body clear and anatomically natural, plus a simple pressure-control valve and insulated support. It must match the boiler in the main view.
No labels, words, diagrams, border, new scenery, combat or extra machines. 1536x1024 landscape. This is a proposed steam-powered revision for review, not an automatic approved reference.

jobs.title: Hush pavilion
jobs.test: Can healing be shared across a group without becoming an invulnerable protective dome?
jobs.lean: Open; faith-led or communal healing traditions
jobs.notes: Several healers sustain quiet restorative magic across a field-care pavilion. Tests collective reach and coordination while keeping the effect about care.
jobs.brief:
Input is a positive reference for warm, humane healing magic and practical modest kit. Do not copy the same old healer, censer, luminous bandage or exact costume.
A simple open-sided field-care pavilion about EIGHT metres across, with a low linen canopy on SIX real wooden posts and visible guy ropes. A few plain woven mats, three low cots and ordinary jars belong to this installation, all physically sized correctly. A calm group of THREE adult healers in varied plain ivory/ochre/blue work clothes attends THREE resting clothed adult patients. One healer at the front is a mature woman with a broad natural face and short curly grey hair; no one is glamorized. No injury detail, blood or dramatic pain.
The healers hold their hands near individual patients; warm ivory-gold light gathers softly around the hands and follows slow breath-like arcs from one care pair to the next. The distributed effect links the healers' effort and gives a quiet sense of shared restorative warmth. Magic is visibly from the people and their cooperation, not the tent poles, fuel jars, a written spell battery or captive spirit. Absolutely NO golden shield extension, dome, force wall, armor made of light or barrier enclosing the pavilion.
Two small detail studies: (1) a healer's hands poised above a patient's clothed wrist, with the warm restrained shared healing light; (2) a plain roll of bandages, ceramic salve jars and soft wool blankets. Whole pavilion visible, neutral backdrop, no war camp or landscape. This is a test of collective magic, not proof that all sickness is cured instantly.

jobs.title: Far-voice station
jobs.test: Can magic carry a voice over distance, and could communities build a network around it?
jobs.lean: Open; scholarly, civic or ritual use
jobs.notes: A large resonant bell installation sends speech to a distant partner. Tests a different kind of power: information and coordination rather than lifting or damage.
jobs.brief:
One substantial civic communications instrument roughly SIX metres high: an exposed simple oak belfry supports a single enormous muted-bronze resonating bell, its broad mouth angled diagonally downward toward a HUMAN-SIZED speaking station. Two heavy stone footings and braced oak posts carry the weight coherently. An adult attendant in an ordinary brown-blue wool coat speaks softly toward a smaller matching bronze mouthpiece connected to the bell frame by ONE slender tensioned silver wire. Another adult listens with a hand near the stone support. Their 1.7-metre height makes the bell's size readable.
Fine blue-violet standing-wave ripples softly illuminate the bell mouth, with the suggestion of a human voice passing through AIR, not faces projected in glass. No goggles, optical lenses, mirrors, screens, readable floating text, skull microphones, electronics or scroll cassettes. jobs.title: Storm-drawing mast
jobs.test: How far may people redirect natural forces, and how much structure and cooperation should it take?
jobs.lean: Open; instinctive storm magic meeting organized craft
jobs.notes: A crew attempts to draw a passing storm through a monumental mast into a mechanical drive. The largest power test: dangerous natural force shaped collectively.
jobs.brief:
Input references the compelling white-violet STORM ENERGY on rough iron, not the same orc character, hook-spear, clothes or composition.
A monumental storm-drawing installation about TWENTY metres tall, fully visible: one tapered dark oak-and-iron mast with three long plain curved wrought-iron prongs at its top, THREE massive angled support braces anchored to wide stone footings, and a large simple grounded flywheel at the base. The shapes should be legible and believable, not a Gothic tower, modern electric pylon, radar antenna, coil forest or Tesla laboratory.
A passing little fragment of storm cloud is implied just above the mast tip against otherwise warm neutral paper. A single powerful white-violet lightning arc is being drawn from that fragment into the iron prongs, then narrows into a visible contained spiral of WIND and force beside the mast down toward the flywheel. Use painterly high-fantasy light, not neon circuit lines or a solid glowing cable. FOUR tiny but realistically scaled adult workers/casters at the base brace and coordinate at plain hand controls; one bare-handed caster guides a short branch of the same storm force. Mixed personal work clothes of one local community, no parade of fantasy races. Small faded red cloth ties are one person's belongings, not a faction banner.
Two detail studies: (1) one large plain iron prong and its restrained top junction; (2) the grounded flywheel and hand-control station, with an adult operator for scale. No scrolls, rune batteries, giant automaton, fortress, surrounding city, war or destroyed landscape. Capture awe and controlled danger. This is deliberately the outer edge of the review batch; it does not establish that weather-scale power is routine or safe.
